method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across divine utterance and servitude, the voice on Sinai and the promised revelation, reciprocal testimony, the Tree, Temple, Pen and Book, creative speech and disclosure, hearing and recognition, objections and discernment, sovereignty within imprisonment and grief, personal letters and remembered visits, prayer as answer, and the consequences of hearing. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. Imported wording checked separately; version differences remain explicit. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.text: Verily I am God, no God is there but Me, and aught except Me is but My creation. Say, worship Me then, O ye, My creatures.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Verily I am the Proof of God and His Light
selected.reason: Seal of the Báb reading “Verily I am the Proof of God and His Light”; a terse inscription of the Báb’s claim.

selected.text: I am He Who speaketh from Mine all-highest horizon
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s word “I am He Who speaketh from Mine all-highest horizon”; the first-person voice prayer answers.

selected.text: There is none other God but Me, the Rememberer and the Remembered
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s word “There is none other God but Me, the Rememberer and the Remembered”; the divine name suited to remembrance.

selected.text: Verily the Throne is My Temple whereon the All-Merciful is seated.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the Throne is His Temple whereon the All-Merciful is seated; joins the Throne and Temple images.

selected.text: Today He Who conversed with Moses is seated upon the throne of Revelation
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s brief statement that today He Who conversed with Moses is seated upon the throne of Revelation; the Sinai claim at its simplest.

selected.text: God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, and that I am He
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s brief testimony that God bears witness there is no God but Him “and that I am He”; the shortest statement of identity in the guide.

selected.text: By My Word were the heavens raised up, and by My Name was the Throne established
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that by His Word the heavens were raised and by His Name the Throne established; the opening claim of creative speech.

selected.text: "O peoples of the earth! The Lord of Heaven hath come with manifest sovereignty."
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s proclamation that the Lord of Heaven has come with manifest sovereignty; the summons that the closing call to action answers.

selected.text: Thou didst manifest the Manifestation of Thyself through Thy sovereignty and Thy power
selected.reason: Prayer acknowledging that God manifested His Manifestation through His sovereignty; prayer recognizing the Manifestation.

selected.text: Verily We have manifested Ourselves for your life, but most of the people are heedless
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s word that He manifested Himself for their life though most are heedless; the purpose of the voice.

selected.text: "Verily, I am the Truth! It hath been written from God as a proof for all the worlds."
selected.reason: The Báb’s declaration, written as a proof for all the worlds, “Verily, I am the Truth!”; a brief proclamation from a letter to a Temple.

selected.text: the call of the All-Merciful on this Naw-Ruz wherein all things have been adorned with the raiment of My remembrance
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s mention of the call of the All-Merciful on a Naw-Rúz when all things were adorned with His remembrance; a festival occasion of address.

selected.text: Were He to find mighty servants, He would forever and always proclaim "Verily, I am God!"
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that, were He to find mighty servants, He would forever proclaim “Verily, I am God!”; shows the bearing of hearers’ capacity on what is said.

selected.text: O people! I am the Most Great Sign amongst you and the Most Exalted Word within you.
selected.reason: Lawh-i-Quds declaring, “I am the Most Great Sign amongst you and the Most Exalted Word within you”; a concise claim to be the Word.

selected.text: The Wronged One hath loved faithfulness and hath ever gazed and continueth to gaze upon it
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s word that the Wronged One has loved faithfulness and ever gazes upon it; faithfulness named in the closing readings.

selected.text: The Beloved hath come with sovereignty, grandeur and glory. Beware that ye oppose Him not.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s warning that the Beloved has come with sovereignty and glory, and bidding none oppose Him; a brief warning against opposition.

selected.text: Verily this is the Manifestation of God in all things, as every created thing doth testify
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that this is the Manifestation of God in all things, as every created thing testifies; creation’s testimony.

selected.text: I have come to you from Sinai with the call of God, the Exalted, the Triumphant, the Ancient
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s first-person statement, “I have come to you from Sinai with the call of God”; a direct personal form of the Sinai claim.

selected.text: All names are My name and whatsoever is created is My proof - blessed are they who know.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that all names are His name and whatsoever is created is His proof; a memorable universal claim.

selected.text: We departed in such glory as the eyes of them that are nigh unto God had never beheld the like
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s word that He departed in such glory as those nigh unto God had never beheld; exile seen as glory.

selected.text: We have offered up one of Our Branches. Say: Unto Thee be praise, O Glory of the worlds
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s words “We have offered up one of Our Branches” with praise to the Glory of the worlds; grief at sacrifice within the divine voice.

selected.text: He is the One Who hath rolled up the heavens of your idle fancies while ye perceive it not.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of the One Who rolled up the heavens of idle fancies while people perceive it not; a memorable reply to vain imaginings.

selected.text: He hath appeared in the garment of "I am" and speaketh forth with "I am the One Who is manifest."
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing Him Who appeared in the garment of “I am” and speaks with “I am the One Who is manifest”; names the first person as a garment.

selected.text: O thou who art mentioned before the Wronged One! Bear thou witness even as God hath borne witness
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding one mentioned before the Wronged One to bear witness even as God has borne witness; the hearer called to answering testimony.

selected.text: Thou art the Lord, Thou art the Creator, Thou art the One Who appeared on Sinai in the realm of lights.
selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá addressing the One Who appeared on Sinai in the realm of lights; a prayer answering the Sinai voice.

selected.text: We call them to the Kawthar of life, but they have turned away from it, having followed vain imaginings.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh lamenting that He calls them to the Kawthar of life but they turn away after vain imaginings; refusal of the offered life.

selected.text: I am God, there is none other God but Me, verily, I am, at all times independent of the entire creation
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declaring that He is God and is at all times independent of the entire creation; the first-person claim to independence.

selected.text: Now is the time for the diffusion of light and the manifestation of mysteries from the Revealer of Sinai
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s statement that now is the time for diffusion of light and manifestation of mysteries from the Revealer of Sinai; carries the Sinai theme into the call to action.

selected.text: I am so fatigued the hour is come when I must leave everything and take My flight. I am too weary to walk.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: The Supreme Pen testifieth that thou hast recognized My sovereignty and drawn from the ocean of My knowledge
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s word that the Supreme Pen testifies that the hearer has recognized His sovereignty and drawn from His ocean of knowledge; recognition attested.

selected.text: I was a Treasure hidden in a station unknown to all save Mine own Self, the All-Knowing, the All-Informed
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Thus doth the Pen move when the Tongue of Eternity speaketh. He, verily, is the Single One, the All-Knowing.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that thus the Pen moves when the Tongue of Eternity speaks; a compact relation of Pen and Tongue.

selected.text: the Speaker on Sinai hath proclaimed: "There is none other God but Me, the Lord of the unseen and the seen."
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the Speaker on Sinai has proclaimed there is none other God but Him, Lord of the unseen and the seen; Sinai in the invitation to hear.

selected.text: This is a letter from God, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting, unto God, the Almighty, the Best Beloved
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: O My Pen! How many a day hast thou heard My lamentation for My tribulations and thy cry for Mine afflictions!
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asking His Pen how many a day it has heard His lamentation for His tribulations; grief shared with the Pen.

selected.text: I created creation for this Day, yet when it appeared, those who followed vain imaginings turned away from it
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s word that He created creation for this Day yet those who followed vain imaginings turned away; the purpose of creation and its refusal.

selected.text: God hath made Me the Discriminator between created things - verily He is the Ruler over whatsoever He willeth
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s word that God made Him the Discriminator between created things; recognition as the criterion of discernment.

selected.text: Behold naught save My luminous and exalted Beauty, and utter naught save My praise, if thou be of them that know.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s counsel to behold naught save His luminous Beauty and utter naught save His praise; speech as response.

selected.text: This is a Book that speaketh the truth, that there is none other God but Him, the Almighty, the Self-Subsisting.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing a Book that speaks the truth that there is none other God but Him; begins the second reading with utterance attributed to the Book itself.

selected.text: O concourse of creation! The gates of heaven have been opened through this Lamp that hath appeared in human temple
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh announcing that the gates of heaven have opened through this Lamp that has appeared in human temple; joins presence and the human form.

selected.text: "Verily, there is none other God but Me, the Mighty, the All-Knowing." I created all peoples for this Most Great Day
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s declaration with the word “I created all peoples for this Most Great Day”; the purpose of creation tied to the present Day.

selected.text: And I am He Who speaketh in all things that I am God, there is no God but Me, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Generous
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s first-person word, “I am He Who speaketh in all things that I am God”; identifies the Speaker with the universal voice.

selected.text: This is a Book which of itself speaketh and saith, heareth and answereth. Verily He is the Speaker, the All-Hearing.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing a Book that of itself speaks, hears and answers; the Book as living voice, as the introduction describes.

selected.text: This is an epistle from the One Who hath been imprisoned in the path of God, the Almighty, the Powerful, the Bestower
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing an epistle from the One imprisoned in the path of God; a letter naming its imprisoned author.

selected.text: the Lote-Tree of the utmost boundary proclaimeth: "There is none other God but I, the All-Hearing, the All-Answering."
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of the Lote-Tree proclaiming God as the All-Hearing, the All-Answering; the voice that also hears and answers.

selected.text: This is a Day wherein all things speak even as the Ancient Beauty spoke when He was seated upon His Most Great Throne.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing a Day wherein all things speak even as the Ancient Beauty spoke upon His Throne; universal speech following divine utterance.

selected.text: The Tongue of Revelation hath spoken: Verily, there is none other God but Him, the All-Compelling, the Self-Subsisting.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the Tongue of Revelation has spoken that there is none other God but Him; the representative form of the Tongue’s proclamation.

selected.text: These are the days of the All-Merciful, and the lamp of divine favor is lit and shining at the axis of contingent being.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s word that these are the days of the All-Merciful and the lamp of divine favour shines at the axis of being; frames the letters with the days of the All-Merciful.

selected.text: The Wronged One calls out amidst the world and commands the people to that which He was commanded by the Mighty, the Wise.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing the Wronged One commanding the people to what He was commanded by the Mighty, the Wise; commanded speech becoming command.

selected.text: Today the Speaker of Sinai is manifest and evident, and upon the branches of the Divine Lote-Tree He speaks and proclaims.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declaring that the Speaker of Sinai is manifest today and speaks upon the branches of the Divine Lote-Tree; joins Sinai and the Tree.

selected.text: God hath dawned forth from the horizon of the Prison upon thee, O thou who hast turned towards God, the Cleaver of the Dawn!
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s word that God has dawned forth from the horizon of the Prison upon the one who turned to Him; light from the prison.

selected.text: We love to remember the loved ones in all conditions, as attested by that which hath been sent down from My Most Exalted Pen
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s word that He loves to remember the loved ones in all conditions; affection in remembrance.

selected.text: O My servants! Hearken unto My call from the precincts of My prison. There is none other God but I, the Stranger, the Prisoner.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh calling His servants from His prison, “There is none other God but I, the Stranger, the Prisoner”; the striking conjunction that opens the prison readings.

selected.text: Hearken thou unto the call of thy Lord from the right side of the Throne, from behind a thousand veils of luminous silk damask.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh calling the hearer to the call of the Lord from behind a thousand veils of luminous silk damask; a memorable image of mediated hearing.

selected.text: We found man asleep; We awakened him. And We saw him distant; We drew him near. And We found him mute; We caused him to speak
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s “We found man asleep; We awakened him … We found him mute; We caused him to speak”; the awakening of speech in the hearer.

selected.text: We left the house, turning toward another land, remembering My early days and speaking the verses of God, the Lord of the worlds
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing leaving the house for another land, remembering His early days and speaking God’s verses; a human scene of exile.

selected.text: By My life! These shall detach them from the worlds and draw them nigh unto a station wherein the Tree of the Command doth speak: "There is no God but Me, the Powerful, the Exalted, the Mighty, the Beauteous
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s oath that these counsels detach people from the worlds and draw them to the station where the Tree speaks; the effect of heeding.

selected.text: O people! I am but a servant of God and His bondsman. I have come to you from the direction of God with a message from Him.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s direct declaration that He is but a servant of God come with a message from Him; keeps servanthood beside the claims of divinity.

selected.text: "Verily, in every state He speaketh: 'I, verily, am God. There is none other God but Me, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting.'"
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh quoting the words that in every state He speaks, “I, verily, am God … the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting”; the formula of the One Who speaks in every state.

selected.text: We were with thee at the time when thou didst what thou didst in the name of thy Lord. Verily thy Lord is cognizant of all things.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh telling the hearer He was with him when he acted in the Lord’s name; a remembered deed.

selected.text: We summon you unto God and seek from you no recompense - the Pen of Revelation beareth witness to this, were ye of them that hear.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s word that He summons all to God and seeks no recompense; the selflessness of the call.

selected.text: By God! The Fire hath returned in the Tree and speaketh forth: 'I am, verily, God, the Mighty, the Exalted, the Well-Beloved.'
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s oath that the Fire has returned in the Tree and speaks, “I am, verily, God”; a compact image of the burning bush renewed.

selected.text: Thus did the Tongue of Grandeur speak as He walked during this night in a place which God had made among the most exalted of places.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that the Tongue of Grandeur spoke as He walked during this night; an everyday occasion of revelation.

selected.text: This is a Book which speaks with truth and makes mention of the people in this Day … We have offered up Our spirit in the days of God
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing a Book that speaks with truth and adding “We have offered up Our spirit in the days of God”; sacrifice in the closing readings.

selected.text: O Husayn! Hearken unto the Voice of Him Who speaketh in all things: "There is none other God but Me, the Mighty, the All-Bountiful!"
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding Husayn hearken to the Voice of Him Who speaks in all things; a personal summons to hear.

selected.text: My hair is My Messenger. It is calling aloud at all times upon the branch of Fire within the hallowed and luminous garden of Paradise
selected.reason: Tablet of the Hair declaring “My hair is My Messenger” calling upon the branch of Fire; the personified image as messenger.

selected.text: This is a Tablet from the Prisoner … Hearken thou unto My call from the direction of the Prison, that there is none other God but Him
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing a Tablet from the Prisoner bidding the hearer hearken from the Prison that there is none other God but Him; the call that prayer answers.

selected.text: And this, verily, is the Beauty of God which hath dawned from behind the veils with a sovereignty that cannot be concealed nor hidden.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing the Beauty of God dawning from behind the veils with an unconcealable sovereignty; the counterpart of the measured veil.

selected.text: O My Afnan! Recall thou the days when thou wert in My presence and didst hear the voice of God, the King, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding His Afnan recall the days he was in His presence and heard the voice of God; a remembered visit, as the introduction describes.

selected.text: The Dawning-Place of the Divine Books is manifest today, and the Speaker on Sinai uttereth His discourse from the most exalted station.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing the Dawning-Place of the Divine Books as manifest and the Speaker on Sinai uttering His discourse from the most exalted station; links Sinai to all scripture.

selected.text: The trees hear My call in the morning and the evening, at nightfall and at dawn. By My life! In the early hours My ears hear My own call.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh saying the trees hear His call morning and evening and in the early hours His ears hear His own call; opens the section on hearing.

selected.text: Me, therefore, do ye worship. This is a blessed leaf from the Crimson Tree - there is no God but He. Say: Me, therefore, do ye fear.
selected.reason: The Báb in Kitab al-Ruh calling for worship and speaking of a blessed leaf from the Crimson Tree; the Báb’s use of Tree-and-leaf imagery.

selected.text: I am He through Whose name the Tablets were sent down and the pages of God, your Lord, were adorned, were ye of the perceiving ones.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declaring Himself He through Whose name the Tablets were sent down and the pages of God adorned; ties the speaker to all scripture.

selected.text: The Most Great Ocean hath surged, and from each drop thereof is heard: "There is no God but Him, the One, the Mighty, the All-Bountiful!"
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of the Most Great Ocean surging and every drop proclaiming there is no God but Him; the ocean and drops named in the guide’s questions.

selected.text: We have turned toward thee from the precincts of the Prison and have sent down for thee that which will attract thee to the supreme horizon
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh telling the hearer He has turned to him from the Prison and sent what will attract him; personal address from the prison.

selected.text: Blessed art thou for having attained unto My days, and for having heard My Revelation and My establishment upon the throne of My utterance.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh blessing one who attained His days and heard His Revelation and His establishment on the throne of utterance; hearing as attainment.

selected.text: He speaketh as He pleaseth even as He spoke in the Burning Bush - "Verily, there is no God but Me, the All-Knowing, the All-Informed."
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that He speaks as He pleases even as He spoke in the Burning Bush; links hearing to the Sinai voice.

selected.text: O people! I desired not to manifest Myself, but the Mighty, the Faithful manifested Me. I concealed My face; your Ancient Lord revealed it.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh saying He desired not to manifest Himself but the Mighty, the Faithful manifested Him; a memorable statement of revelation as unsought.

selected.text: the Prisoner, through Whom the Tree hath spoken, and the Mount called out, and the Rock cried aloud, and the Vale flowed, and the Dove sang
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh naming the Prisoner through Whom the Tree spoke, the Mount called out and the Dove sang; joins Sinai imagery to the prisoner.

selected.text: I, verily, am the Path of God unto all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth; well is it with them that hasten thereunto!
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: The atoms have testified to that which My tongue hath testified in My prison - that there is none other God but Me, the All-Knowing Speaker.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh saying the atoms testified to what His tongue testified in His prison; joins creation’s witness and prison.

selected.text: My tongue hath testified to My Self, and My Self hath testified to My Temple … Thus hath My tongue spoken in the kingdom of Mine utterance
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that His tongue testified to His Self and His Self to His Temple; a concise chain of self-testimony.

selected.text: Verily the sea walketh in human form and counseleth the servants with that which will profit them in the worlds of their Lord, the All-Wise.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of the sea walking in human form and counselling the servants; a memorable picture of the ocean made human.

selected.text: A remembrance from Us to whoever desires to enter within the pavilion of grandeur and glory … We have loved your presence even as you love it
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s remembrance to whoever desires the pavilion of grandeur: “We have loved your presence even as you love it”; friendship with the Manifestation.

selected.text: We have manifested that which was hidden in knowledge and have sent down from the heaven of Will that which the reckoners have failed to reckon
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing having manifested what was hidden in knowledge and sent down what reckoners failed to reckon; the disclosure prayer receives.

selected.text: By God! I speak not of Mine own desire, but the Spirit speaketh within My breast. These words are not from Me but from One mighty and powerful.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s oath that He speaks not of His own desire but that the Spirit speaks within His breast; the guide’s opening declaration, named in its introduction.

selected.text: We have heard thy mention and have remembered thee. We have found the fragrance of thy love and have sent down for thee this well-beloved Tablet
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh saying He heard the hearer’s mention, found the fragrance of his love and sent this Tablet; the occasion of a Tablet.

selected.text: O people! By God, My tongue moveth through the will of your Lord, the Most Merciful, and My pen through His all-powerful and mighty finger.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh affirming that His tongue moves through the will of the Lord and His pen through His mighty finger; names tongue and pen as instruments of the divine will.

selected.text: The four letters which are mentioned in the tradition of the Imam (peace be upon him) that must be revealed with the Promised One are these four stations: The station of servitude, with which the Promised One arose at first; and the station of Imamate, concerning which He said "Verily I am the Qa'im Whose appearance was promised unto you"; third is the station of Prophethood, concerning which He said that the Holy Manifestations have no beginning and no end; fourth is the word "Verily I am God" - "He speaketh not from mere impulse. His utterance is but revealed revelation."
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explaining the four stations of the Promised One: servitude, Imamate, Prophethood and “Verily I am God”; a systematic account of differing stations of speech.

selected.text: He is the One speaking at the center of the world, that all peoples might turn to the horizon of the manifestation of God, the Lord of all worlds.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing the One speaking at the centre of the world so that all peoples may turn to God’s horizon; the purpose of the declaration.

selected.text: outward being calls unto Mine inward being, and Mine inward being unto Mine outward. There is none in the dominion save Me, and I am the True One, the Knower of things unseen
selected.reason: Seal of Bahá’u’lláh in which His outward being calls unto His inward being and the inward unto the outward; a distinctive image of self-address.

selected.text: act with goodliness. Blessed is he who has heard and acted upon that which he was commanded by the One Who is the Wise Commander. We have forbidden the servants from all that would give rise to sorrows in the contingent world
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh blessing whoever heard and acted on the Wise Commander’s command and forbidding what gives rise to sorrow; action and the avoidance of harm.

selected.text: Were ye to look with My eye, ye would behold it as the Dawning-Place of My most excellent names and the Manifestation of My most exalted attributes
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh telling the hearer that, were he to look with His eye, he would behold the Dawning-Place of His names; seeing with the divine eye.

selected.text: The All-Bountiful, Who is imprisoned in the prison of 'Akka, makes mention of thee, inasmuch as He hath summoned all unto God, the Lord of all names
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing the All-Bountiful imprisoned in Akka mentioning the hearer and summoning all unto God; prison and summons.

selected.text: I have appeared and made manifest that which was recorded in the Books of God and treasured up in His knowledge; yet most of the people are as dead.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that He made manifest what was treasured in the Books of God yet most people are as dead; disclosure met by heedlessness.

selected.text: God hath testified of Himself that there is no God but Him - no God but I, the Single, the One, the Individual, the Self-Subsisting, the Bountiful.
selected.reason: The Báb stating that God has testified of Himself that there is no God but Him, “no God but I”; shows the shift between third and first person in one sentence.

selected.text: The Tree hath spoken in My breast and the Treasure hath called out in My heart, saying: "There is none other God besides Me, the Mighty, the Great."
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh saying the Tree has spoken in His breast and the Treasure called out in His heart; joins Tree and Hidden Treasure inwardly.

selected.text: This is a Book which hath been sent down in truth from the presence of One mighty and wise. It speaketh that I am the Prisoner in this mighty Prison.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing a Book from the mighty and wise that speaks, “I am the Prisoner in this mighty Prison”; the Book voicing imprisonment.

selected.text: By God, I speak not from desire - rather the Spirit speaketh within My breast, and My proof is My arising and what floweth from a mighty holy Finger.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s parallel oath that the Spirit speaks within His breast, adding that His proof is His arising and what flows from a holy Finger; extends the opening declaration to its evidence.

selected.text: I have believed in God and the Manifestations of His Cause. He hath raised Me up in truth and sent Me unto all who are in the heavens and on earth
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh testifying that He believed in God and His Manifestations and was raised up and sent unto all in heaven and earth; joins faith, commission and universality.

selected.text: God testifieth that there is none other God but Him, and He Who speaketh is verily the Dawning-Place of revelation and the Rising-Point of inspiration.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh identifying He Who speaks as the Dawning-Place of revelation and the Rising-Point of inspiration; a representative form of the guide’s testimonial formula.

selected.text: O peoples of the earth! By the True God, the Call hath been raised from the prison of Akka - a Call in whose yearning to hear it countless souls have perished. selected.text: The Lord of Names declareth: The Kingdom belongeth unto God, the Lord of all the worlds. And the Lord of Creation declareth: Glory be unto God, the Object of the mystics. selected.text: The Ancient Countenance hath turned toward thee from this glorious horizon. The servant in attendance before the Throne desired to write unto thee. selected.text: By God! selected.text: God testifieth that there is none other God but Him, and that He Who hath appeared is verily the Most Exalted Pen, the Lote-Tree beyond which there is no passing, the Most Glorious Horizon, the Manifestation of the Unseen in the Kingdom of Creation, the First Exemplar among nations, the Temple manifested in justice, and the Light shining forth from the horizon of grace.

selected.text: O servants!
